steps.instruction: Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/ in the browser. If a login page appears, sign in with username admin and password admin; if Grafana then prompts you to change the admin password, click Skip. Then find and open the dashboard named 'Service health' (use the search in the top bar or the Dashboards browse menu). Once it has loaded, report the exact titles of all panels shown on that dashboard, exactly as displayed, one per line.

steps.instruction: Create a NEW dashboard in Grafana. Add a Stat visualization panel and title it exactly '{{runid}} Availability'. For its query, select the 'TestData' data source (a data source named TestData or 'TestData DB' — pick the one whose name is TestData; if there are multiple test data sources choose the one literally named 'TestData'). Use a simple query such as the 'Random Walk' scenario or default test data so the panel gets data. Then save the dashboard with the title exactly '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' (use the Save dashboard button, set the dashboard name in the save dialog, and confirm the save). Verify the save succeeded (no unsaved-changes indicator) and report the dashboard's URL from the browser address bar, the panel title as shown, and the data source name shown in the panel's query editor.

steps.instruction: On the currently open dashboard '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' (URL http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard), do two things and save: (1) Add the tag 'bench' to the dashboard — use Dashboard settings (gear icon) > General, add 'bench' in the Tags field, then click Save. (2) Set the dashboard's time range to the last 6 hours: open the time picker in the top bar and choose 'Last 6 hours'. Then click Save dashboard; in the save dialog, TICK the checkbox 'Update default time range' so the 6-hour range is persisted into the saved dashboard, and confirm the save. Verify both succeeded: report the tags shown in Dashboard settings > General (or the tag chip visible on the dashboard), the time range shown in the top-bar time picker, and whether the 'Update default time range' checkbox was ticked when saving.

steps.instruction: On the currently open dashboard '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard' (URL http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard), set the dashboard's auto-refresh interval to '1m'. This is configured in Dashboard settings (gear icon) > General section, in the 'Auto refresh interval' field (set it to 1m), then click Save. Alternatively, if it's set via the top-bar refresh picker's 'Refresh every' option, use that and then save the dashboard explicitly with the Save dashboard button. Make sure the change is persisted by saving the dashboard. Verify and report the value shown in the 'Auto refresh interval' field after saving, and confirm the save succeeded (no unsaved-changes indicator).
